newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up across the board on Thursday on short-covering after technical corrections over the past few days, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 23,980 yuan ($2,889) per tonne, rising 80 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 23,950 yuan and hit a high of 24,060 yuan.
April rose 70 to 23,570, May 50 to 23,700, June 80 to 23,980, August 100 to 23,900.
Combined volume fell to 34,710 tonnes from 52,040.
Copper opened higher and moved at high levels for most of the session on short-covering but trading volume fell with most investors taking a wary attitude, traders said.
"Short-covering was responsible for the day's rises, but falls in trading volume indicated many investors remained on the sidelines and the short-term market trend remains unclear," one trader said.
Traders said copper was not likely to rise or fall sharply in the short term for lack of any fresh market-moving news.
Analysts expected copper to continue to consolidate in a narrow range in the next few days.
Aluminium ended mixed. April rose 50 yuan to 16,350 yuan per tonne, May fell 20 to 16,680 and June was down 20 to 16,930.
Combined volume rose to 1,820 tonnes from 920.
